aboutH2: Heritage Treatment Foundation: A Non-12-Step Approach to Addiction Treatment
intro: Heritage Treatment Foundation is a residential treatment center located just an hour away from Montreal that specializes in a non-12-Step approach to addiction treatment. They provide evidence-based treatments that focus on psychotherapy, pharmacotherapy, and alternative therapies to address both addiction and underlying mental health issues. All treatments are personalized to the client’s specific needs.

Heritage Treatment Foundation’s emphasis on positive psychology is vital to their clients’ recovery. They believe that the process of addiction treatment is about reinventing oneself as a happier, sober, stronger person. They work toward this goal by offering a variety of evidence-based therapies like cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), rational emotive behavioural therapy (REBT), psychodynamic therapy, and cognitive bias modification therapy, both in individual and group psychotherapy sessions. Clients with certain conditions may receive medication-assisted treatment.

The Heritage Treatment Foundation’s intimate size allows them to provide more attention to each client. They accept only 12 clients at a time. Their on-site detox, aftercare program, and strong alumni support through weekly meetings ensure that clients are supported throughout their recovery journey.

pillars.title: Comfortable Cottage Home: A Relaxing Place for Healing with Alternative Therapies
pillars.body: Heritage Treatment Foundation’s residential facility offers a comfortable cottage home where clients can relax and heal. The bedrooms are air-conditioned and equipped with high speed internet and a television. Clients are encouraged to participate in various alternative therapies that promote relaxation, wellness, and healing.

pillars.title: Aftercare Meetings, a Recovery App and Virtual Therapy
pillars.body: Before you go home, your assigned therapist helps you put together a post-treatment plan that looks honestly at the situations most likely to trip you up. Once you've left, you and your family can keep coming to the centre's aftercare meetings and use its recovery app. If you want more structure, you can carry on with a counsellor through the virtual outpatient program. Family and couples sessions can be booked too, and relatives who live too far away to visit can join by phone.

pillars.title: A Small Clinical Team That Works as One
pillars.body: Everyone is assigned a therapist on arrival. That therapist writes your treatment plan, prepares any letters you need for a lawyer or a court, and gives you a final report on your progress when you finish. You can also work with other therapists on the team. The centre says its counsellors trained in psychology and addiction at accredited schools, and that staff differ enough in background and personality that most people find someone they click with. Medical detox is overseen by an affiliated physician, and staff are on site around the clock.

overview: Heritage Home Treatment Foundation is a leading residential rehab center situated just a short drive away from Montreal, Quebec, Canada. As a non-profit, non-12-step facility, the center has been offering professional support and care to individuals struggling with addiction issues for several years. The facility accommodates up to 12 residents at any given time, who are embraced in a supportive, private, and serene environment that helps them overcome addiction.

Apart from treating addiction, Heritage Home Treatment Foundation addresses the underlying causes that often fuel addictive behavior by using evidence-based treatments. From psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy to holistic healing techniques that may involve yoga and meditation, every treatment program is individualized to meet the specific needs of each resident. With a focus on lifelong recovery, graduates of the program can look forward to a future full of sobriety, balanced emotional, and mental wellness, and a supportive community network that can help them cope with everyday life.
serviceCaption: 12 services · as described on the centre's website
afterOverview: Heritage Treatment Foundation offers alternative therapies such as yoga, meditation, massage, acupuncture, stress management, art therapy, tai-chi, rituals, and more. These therapies can be combined with evidence-based therapies to create a personalized treatment plan for each client.

Heritage Treatment Foundation also offers various fun activities for clients such as biking, hiking, kayaking, golfing, fishing, geo-trekking, zip-lining, boating, bowling, camping, gardening, local excursions, photography, pottery, and art therapy. These activities and therapies promote relaxation, socialization, stress relief, and overall wellness.

location.heading: Heritage Treatment Foundation in Godmanchester, Quebec
location.intro: The residence is on Route 138 in Godmanchester, a farming township near Huntingdon in Montérégie, roughly an hour and ten minutes by car from downtown Montreal, 25 minutes from Salaberry-de-Valleyfield and a little under two hours from Ottawa. Heritage is the name the foundation uses in Montreal and the rest of Quebec, where English-language residential programs are rare, and it meets families at an office at 1200 McGill College Avenue downtown; people in Ottawa know the same house as Sobriety.ca Foundation.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Heritage Treatment Foundation cost?
faqs.a: The centre doesn't publish its prices, so you'll need to call or email admissions for current rates. Its FAQ lists what isn't included in the program fee: alternative treatments after the first free session, family therapy, medication, and medical or hospital visits. Some recreational outings cost extra, but you never have to join a paid activity.

faqs.q: How long is treatment, and is there medical detox?
faqs.a: The core residential program runs 30 days or longer, and the centre offers stays of 30, 60 or 90 days. Medical detox comes first if you need it: it averages about 7 days, under the direction of an affiliated physician with staff on site 24/7. For withdrawal that is too severe to manage at the residence, the centre says it will help you find a suitable detox facility first, and some people also take up to 48 hours of rest before the full therapy schedule begins.

faqs.q: Where is the centre and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Treatment takes place at 2678 Route 138 in Godmanchester, in the Montérégie region about an hour and ten minutes' drive southwest of downtown Montreal. The foundation also has a meeting office at 1200 McGill College Avenue, Suite 1100, in Montreal. It offers pickups, including set pickup points in Brossard on the South Shore, so ask about transport when you call.

faqs.q: Is treatment in English or French?
faqs.a: Therapy and counselling are in English. The centre describes itself as one of the few English-speaking rehabs in Quebec, and says bilingual and French-speaking residents have also taken part in its programs.

You leave with a post-treatment plan written with your assigned therapist. Graduates and their families can join the centre's aftercare meetings and use its recovery app, and you can continue counselling through its virtual outpatient program.

faqs.q: Can I use insurance, and is this covered by RAMQ?
faqs.a: This is a fee-based, not-for-profit centre, separate from the public CISSS and CIUSSS addiction services, and it doesn't list which insurers cover a residential stay, so check with your plan and with admissions. For its virtual outpatient therapy, the centre says it accepts insurance. Canadian residents should bring their health card so medical visits during treatment aren't billed to them.

faqs.q: Is Heritage the same centre as Sobriety.ca Foundation?
faqs.a: Yes, it is the same residence. Both the Heritage website and sobriety.ca give 2678 Route 138 in Godmanchester as the treatment address. The foundation markets the house to Montreal and Quebec clients as Heritage Home or Heritage Treatment Foundation, and to Ottawa clients as Sobriety.ca Foundation, with separate phone lines and offices for each.
